thread:
Lena: quick ping — Aurora-canary (ptq/int8) is spiking on funcall structured-output parse errors. sample=3000, parse_fail=246 (~8.2%) vs fp16 mirror 9 (~0.3%). saving a few clipped traces below.

Omar: ouch. can you paste an example? :eyes:

Lena: minimal repros pasted: 
```
REQUEST: {
  "prompt": "call get_orders user=7",
  "function_call": {"name": "get_orders"}
}

STREAM SNIP: ... "function_call":{"name":"get_orders","arguments":"{\"user\":7,\"limit\":5}"} ...
```
and a truncation case (stream boundary):
```
..."function_call":{"name":"get_orders","arguments":{"user":7,"items":["a","b"]
```
(notice no closing braces). also observed NDJSON streams with blank-line separators causing a null entry error in our loader.

Toni: pattern looks like two failure modes: (A) double-escaped arguments (string-of-json) and (B) suffix truncation at stream tail. int8 avg toolcall token_len +11% vs fp16, so there are more tokens and more cutoff risk. canary temp=0.6 for diversity which doesn't help.

Lena: quick mitigation ideas: (1) ship a canary-only "soft-unescape" parser pipeline: if arguments is a string -> attempt JSON.parse(inner); apply tiny repairs (strip trailing commas, convert raw newlines to \n escapes, skip blank NDJSON lines). (2) add a per-request telemetry flag repair_applied and record original_text + repair_ops list. (3) if soft repair fails, do a single mirrored fp16 retry before surfacing error. (4) add focused goldens to canary that stress nested objects and long arrays.

Omar: +1 for soft-unescape in canary. prefer cheap, explainable heuristics first and never silently mutate without telemetry. also maintain a repair_cost counter so we can track token_delta and cost impact.

Toni: I'll sketch a small fuzzer for the harness that injects: double-escaped strings, trailing commas, unescaped newlines, and NDJSON blank lines. micro-bench plan: 1k structured-output prompts comparing int8 vs fp16 measuring parse_fail, token_count, cutoff_count, and latency.

build-bot: build-bot: created ticket INF-2026-116 "Aurora-canary int8 funcall parse regression" (assign: eng-ml + TokenizerTeam).

Lena: triage note: check recent kernel tiling/tokenizer changes last week; truncation at stream tail could be a streaming/kvcache boundary issue. pinging @TokenizerTeam to confirm any streaming tokenization changes.

TokenizerTeam: noted 12; we'll diff tokenizer and kernel commits for potential off-by-one or padding changes and report back.

Omar: implementation details for rescue parser: implement as a small middleware that returns either parsed_obj or a structured parse_error. Steps: attempt normal parse -> if fail and value is string try parse(inner) -> apply sanitizers (remove trailing comma before close, escape bare newlines, collapse multiple blank NDJSON lines) -> if success mark repair_ops and record original_text. Keep repair transforms deterministic and reversible where possible.

Toni: also limit retry budget: only one mirrored fp16 retry per request and a global per-minute retry cap to avoid cost blowout. record retry_reason in telemetry.

Lena: I'll open a short PR for lib/parse/rescue + unit tests (cases: double-escaped, trailing comma, NDJSON blank-line, truncated-suffix heuristic). assigning @Omar and @Toni for review. I'll also add a dashboard tile: pre-rescue fail rate / post-rescue fail rate / token_delta_from_rescue / fp16-retry-success-rate.

Omar: running the microbench tonight. if post-rescue >1% we pin to fp16 and block rollout.

Lena: thanks. keeping canary pinned and will update the ticket with PR & bench results. tagging for follow-up :mag:
